concept.name: Retail sales
concept.definition: The monthly estimate of receipts at U.S. retail and food-services establishments, published by the Census Bureau through the Advance Monthly Retail Trade Survey (MARTS) and the Monthly Retail Trade Survey (MRTS). It is the earliest broad indicator of consumer spending on goods.
concept.intuition: Because consumer spending is the largest component of GDP, the retail-sales report is a fast proxy for the health of household demand.
concept.mechanics: The Census Bureau samples retail firms from its business register and collects sales for the reference month; an advance estimate from early respondents is released about two weeks after month-end and revised in the full MRTS, with all headline figures seasonally adjusted and reported in nominal dollars.
concept.failure_modes: Figures are nominal, so inflation inflates them; they cover goods and food services but miss most services spending, and the advance estimate is revised heavily once full MRTS data arrive.
concept.misconceptions: Retail sales are not total consumer spending - services such as housing, healthcare, and travel are largely excluded - so the series understates and skews the true consumption picture.
concept.example: U.S. retail and food-services sales fell 8.7% in March 2020 as lockdowns began, then a record drop, and rebounded more than 18% in May 2020, the largest monthly gain on record.

citations.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Monthly Retail Trade
